questionText: A partnership firm having partners X and Y (Firm #21) with capitals of Rs. 800,000 and Rs. 400,000 suffered a net loss of Rs. 70,000 during the year. The deed provides for interest on capital @ 6% p.a. but does not specify whether it is a charge or appropriation. What is the amount of interest on capital allowable?

options.text: No interest on capital will be allowed to any partner
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

options.text: Full interest of Rs. 48,000 and Rs. 24,000 will be paid creating further loss
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Full interest of Rs. 48,000 and Rs. 24,000 will be paid creating further loss'.

options.text: Interest will be allowed only to A as senior partner

options.text: Interest will be credited to Current Account only
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Interest will be credited to Current Account only'.

detailedSolution:
1. Interest on capital is an appropriation of profit. When the firm incurs a net loss (here Rs. 70,000), no interest on capital can be allowed unless the partnership deed expressly provides that interest on capital is a charge against profits.

topic: Admission of Partner: New Profit Sharing Ratio
questionText: In Firm Case #16, partners X and Y share profits in the ratio of 3:2. They admit Z as a new partner for 1/7th share in the profits. Calculate the new profit sharing ratio among X, Y, and Z.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor '12:18:5'.
Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor '3:2:1'.
Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor '19:11:5'.
Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

detailedSolution:
1. Let total future profit = 1.
   - Incoming partner Z's share = 1/7.
   - Remaining profit share = 1 - 1/7 = 6/7.
2. Old ratio of X and Y is 3:2.
   - New share of X = 3/5 x 6/7 = 18/35.
   - New share of Y = 2/5 x 6/7 = 12/35.
   - New share of Z = 1/7 = 5/35.
3. New Profit Sharing Ratio = 18:12:5.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Dissolution of a Partnership Firm
topic: Dissolution of Firm: Realisation Expenses
questionText: On dissolution of Firm #25: Realisation expenses of Rs. 17,000 were borne by the firm, but paid by partner D on behalf of the firm. What is the journal entry in the firm's books?

options.text: Realisation A/c Dr. to D's Capital A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

options.text: D's Capital A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'D's Capital A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c'.

options.text: D's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'D's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c'.

options.text: Bank A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Bank A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c'.

detailedSolution:
1. Accounting Treatment of Dissolution Expenses:
   - When expenses are borne by firm and paid by firm -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Bank A/c.
   - When borne by partner and paid by firm -> Partner's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c.
   - When borne by partner and paid by partner personally -> No entry in firm's books.
   - When borne by firm and paid by partner -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Partner's Capital A/c.
   - Remuneration allowed to partner -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Partner's Capital A/c.
Hence, Option A is correct.

topic: Dissolution of Firm: Transfer to Realisation Account
questionText: In Dissolution Case #1: How is Partner's Loan Account (loan advanced by partner to firm) treated at the time of closing the books of the firm?

options.text: Transferred directly to Bank Account for payment, NOT to Realisation Account
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Transferred to Partner's Current Account'.

detailedSolution:
1. Rules for Transfer to Realisation Account on Dissolution:
   - All third party liabilities (including Mrs. Partner's Loan and Employees' Provident Fund) are transferred to Realisation A/c (Credit).
   - Partner's own loan is an internal debt paid after third party debts but before capital, and is NOT transferred to Realisation A/c.
   - Goodwill is an asset transferred to Realisation A/c (Debit) at book value.
   - Gross Debtors are debited and Provision for Doubtful Debts is credited to Realisation A/c.
Hence, Option A is correct.
